stage: Captain America again, with the shield Tony gives back. In the end passes his shield to Sam Wilson

verdicts.why: Tony returns the shield and Steve fights as Captain America through Endgame, so 'Gives up the name' is false there. But the shield Steve hands Sam is a second shield (the first is broken in the battle), so 'hands it to Sam' is off; the amended value says 'his shield'.

Natasha dies on Vormir in Endgame, and the box's status row already says so. Affiliation keeps 'Natasha: the Avengers' until the post-credits stage, and the log's later affiliation stages use 'Natasha: deceased'.

From Agent Carter S1 the war is over (per the log's own status row) and the SSR, then S.H.I.E.L.D., are U.S. agencies. The World Security Council first appears on screen at The Consultant, so 'The Allied war effort' is false from Agent Carter S1.

At the end of S3, six months later, Coulson is no longer director. Mace announces S.H.I.E.L.D. as a legitimate organization again only during S4, so 'in secret, under a new director' holds until the S4 stage.
Vol. 3 ends with Quill leaving, Rocket made captain of the new Guardians, Gamora back with the Ravagers, and only Nebula and Drax staying on Knowhere. So 'Knowhere' no longer fits the group.
Multiverse of Madness has no Avengers. It ends with Kamar-Taj being repaired and the surviving sorcerers, joined by America Chavez, training there again.
Bucky falls during the capture of Zola, dated February 1945. On screen in The Winter Soldier, Zola says the Captain took him prisoner in 1945.
Ant-Man's post-credits scene shows Steve and Sam holding Bucky. They can't call Tony because of the accords, so 'Bucky: missing' is false by the end of Ant-Man.
Thor's post-credits scene shows an invisible Loki, who survived his fall and reached Earth, prompting Selvig. His real status at the end of Thor is alive, and Thor itself shows it.

stage: Its name stolen by Aldrich Killian. Real and active: one of its members breaks Trevor Slattery out of prison to meet its leader

verdicts.why: The stage is missing: Norriss reveals the real Ten Rings and breaks Slattery out to meet its leader. But one member does it alone (Norriss kills the guards himself), not 'its agents'.

'The Mandarin, played by actor Trevor Slattery' stays true after All Hail the King, which still treats Slattery as the man who played the Mandarin. The real leader's existence is a status change, covered by item 9, not a false alias.

The Ms. Marvel stage ends with Kamala vanishing as Captain Marvel appears in her room. Wakanda Forever does not show her, and where she went is only shown in The Marvels, so 'active' shows that later title early.
In Blade: Trinity, King and Abigail invite Blade to join their vampire hunters, named on screen as the Nightstalkers, and he fights with them to the end. Place this stage before item 13's stage.

Blade: The Series follows Trinity in the same continuity but has Blade working with Krista Starr and Shen, with no Nightstalkers, so the original value holds again. It goes right after item 12's Blade: Trinity stage (box order), even though both items say insert_after 0.
